standard.title: Present findings and viewpoints
standard.description: present descriptions and explanations, drawing ideas, findings and viewpoints from sources, and using relevant terms and conventions
standard.prior_knowledge: From AC9HS4S07 (Present sourced explanations): Students present descriptions and explanations drawing on sources and using subject-specific terms. Students can present basic sourced accounts at Year 4 level.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students present descriptions and explanations that draw ideas, findings and viewpoints from sources, using relevant subject-specific terms and conventions appropriate to the HASS disciplines.

nodes.label: Drawing from sources in presentations
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can select and reference ideas, findings and viewpoints from sources in their descriptions and explanations, distinguishing their own ideas from source material.
nodes.minimum_width: Present one description or explanation that references at least one source, distinguishing the source's viewpoint from their own.
nodes.typical_width: Select and reference ideas and viewpoints from a range of sources (letters, graphs, tables, timelines, photographs, pictures) in descriptions and explanations, clearly indicating the sources of ideas and distinguishing sourced information from personal interpretation.
wider: Construct a description that synthesises information from three or more sources, weaving together multiple viewpoints into a coherent account
Evaluate how selecting different sources changes the account that can be presented — exploring how source selection is itself a form of perspective-taking
nodes.hinge_reason: Students who present findings without referencing sources cannot demonstrate evidence-based thinking or the distinction between personal opinion and sourced finding. Explicit source attribution is foundational for credible HASS communication.

response_modes.reason: Consistent source attribution is a practice skill that requires reinforcement — students often need repeated feedback to habituate citing sources within their explanations rather than treating references as an afterthought.

success_criteria: Students reference at least one source within their description or explanation.
Students distinguish source-derived information from their own interpretation.

nodes.label: Using subject-specific terms accurately
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can use accurate, subject-specific terms from relevant HASS disciplines in their presentations, applying terms correctly in context.
nodes.minimum_width: Use at least four subject-specific HASS terms correctly in a description or explanation.
nodes.typical_width: Use accurate and subject-appropriate terms across HASS disciplines: historical terms (colonial, gold era, migration, penal), geographic terms (characteristics, environmental, human, ecosystems, sustainable, settlement, management), civics terms (electoral process, democracy, shared beliefs), and economic terms (scarcity, choices, resources, needs and wants).
wider: Develop a HASS glossary of key terms for a unit and use the glossary to improve the precision of a draft explanation
Compare how the same concept is named differently across HASS disciplines (e.g. 'community' in history versus geography versus civics) and explain why disciplinary vocabulary matters

response_modes.reason: Subject-specific vocabulary is a precision skill — incorrect or inconsistent use undermines the credibility of explanations. Students benefit from targeted vocabulary practice embedded in content rather than isolated word lists.

success_criteria: Students use at least four subject-specific HASS terms correctly in context.
Terms are drawn from at least two HASS discipline areas.

nodes.label: Descriptions and explanations in different formats
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can present HASS descriptions and explanations in a range of formats appropriate to purpose and audience, selecting format based on content and communication goals.
nodes.minimum_width: Present findings in one format (written, oral or visual) appropriate to the inquiry purpose.
nodes.typical_width: Present descriptions and explanations in formats suited to purpose: written descriptions, oral explanations, visual displays (maps, timelines, graphs), or multimodal presentations that combine text, image and data.
wider: Produce a multimodal presentation (combining written, oral and visual formats) that communicates HASS findings to a specific audience
Evaluate how different presentation formats (e.g. a written report versus a visual display versus an oral presentation) communicate different aspects of the same findings, and justify a format choice

response_modes.reason: Varied presentation formats build communicative flexibility — students who only practise written formats are poorly equipped for oral or visual communication tasks. Build repertoire across formats across the year.

success_criteria: Students present findings in a format appropriate to the inquiry purpose.
Students explain why their chosen format suits the content and audience.

nodes.label: Presenting evidence-supported descriptions and explanations
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can present descriptions and explanations that draw ideas, findings and viewpoints from sources, use subject-specific terms accurately, and are communicated in a format appropriate to purpose and audience.
nodes.minimum_width: Present a description or explanation that references at least two sources, uses appropriate subject-specific terms, and is in a format suited to the purpose.
nodes.typical_width: Present descriptions and explanations that: draw on sourced ideas and viewpoints across a HASS topic, use accurate subject-specific terms from relevant disciplines, apply appropriate conventions for the chosen format, and communicate findings in a way suited to purpose and audience.
wider: Present findings from an extended HASS inquiry in a form suitable for a real audience (e.g. a school assembly presentation, an article for a school newsletter, a letter to a local council)
Reflect on the effectiveness of a completed presentation — evaluate what communicated well and what could be improved, and identify specific revisions that would strengthen it

response_modes.reason: The integrated presentation task brings together source referencing, disciplinary vocabulary and format selection. Students need to coordinate all three simultaneously — scaffold with a planning template before drafting.

success_criteria: Students reference at least two sources in their description or explanation.
Students use subject-specific HASS terms accurately across at least two discipline areas.
Students present in a format that is appropriate for the content and clearly communicated.
